overview.text: Reykjavík is Iceland’s capital and most populous municipality, on the country’s southwest coast. Its name means “Smoky Bay,” referring to steam rising from nearby hot springs; geothermal water is also used to heat homes and swimming pools. The city is linked to Iceland’s earliest settlement: archaeological remains in its centre date to around 870. The traditional story that Ingólfur Arnarson chose the site by following pillars cast into the sea is a legend, not a confirmed account. Reykjavík’s urban growth began in the 18th century, and it received town rights in 1786. Government offices moved there in 1904, when it became Iceland’s capital and an important national centre.

key_facts.text: Reykjavík is Iceland’s capital and most populous municipality.
The name Reykjavík means “Smoky Bay,” linked to steam from the area’s hot springs.
Archaeological remains in the city centre date to around 870; the story of Ingólfur Arnarson following pillars to the site is presented as legend.
Reykjavík received town rights in 1786, after urban settlement began taking shape there in the 18th century.
Reykjavík became Iceland’s capital in 1904, when government offices were established there after Iceland gained Home Rule.
Geothermal water is used to heat homes and swimming pools in the city.
